text:
I added `slugify(title)` to the `shop` package for PAY-4101, with tests. All 14 tests pass.

- **`src/shop/slug.py`** (new): lowercases the input, replaces each run of non-`[a-z0-9]` characters with one `-`, then strips leading and trailing `-`.
- **`src/shop/__init__.py`**: exports `slugify`, so `from shop import slugify` works.
- **`tests/test_slugify.py`** (new): parametrized cases for spaces, punctuation, repeated separators, digits, empty input, and non-ASCII text, plus a check that output contains only ASCII letters, digits, and single dashes.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`**: added an entry under Unreleased.

Decisions you may want to change:
- I put the function in its own module rather than `core.py`, and re-exported it from the package root.
- Non-ASCII letters are treated as separators, so `café au lait` becomes `caf-au-lait`. That follows the spec literally.

The repo isn't a git repository, so I didn't commit anything. pytest wasn't installed on the system, so I ran the tests from a venv at `/tmp/pr2-venv`.
prompt: Add a new feature called slugify to this package (ticket PAY-4101). It should provide slugify(title): lowercase the text, replace every run of characters that are not ASCII letters or digits with a single '-', and strip leading and trailing '-'. Also add tests.
